title: Container ensure-guard needs a claude auth-preflight before dispatching workers in container mode
description: runContainerEnsureGuard / ensureWorkerContainer (src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts; src/commands/sidecar.ts:3331-3368) re-asserts firewall, config, and toolchain on every ensure but NOT claude auth. A worker_isolation=container sidecar can therefore dispatch an implementer/reviewer/planner worker (docker exec -it cam-worker claude ...) into a container where claude is unauthenticated; the worker fails at runtime instead of a clean fail-closed preflight -- a silent wedge that undermines CAM-139 (autonomous meta-loop requires trustworthy container mode). Discovered live during the CAM-175 ceremony 2026-07-22: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN was commented out in .env, so `docker exec cam-worker claude auth status --json` returned loggedIn:false/authMethod:none; after setting the token and recreating the container it returned loggedIn:true/authMethod:oauth_token. Fix: add an auth-preflight to the container ensure path that runs `docker exec cam-worker claude auth status --json`, parses loggedIn (the codebase's own auth-probe convention, src/commands/run-auth-preflight.ts:72-73), and on loggedIn:false fails closed -- write a durable stall marker mirroring the FirewallError path (.claude/.cam-sidecar-stalled.json, reason container-auth-unavailable) and abort so no worker dispatches, matching the FirewallError/ContainerConfigError/ToolchainMismatchError fail-closed handling at sidecar.ts:3344-3368.

spec.scope: Add a claude auth-preflight to the worker_isolation=container ensure path so the sidecar fails closed (never dispatches a worker) when claude is unauthenticated inside the cam-worker container. Today ensureWorkerContainer re-asserts toolchain, firewall, and config on every ensure but NOT auth, so a container-mode sidecar can dispatch an implementer/reviewer/planner worker into an unauthenticated container and the worker fails at runtime instead of a clean preflight -- a silent wedge that undermines CAM-139 (autonomous meta-loop needs trustworthy container mode). Mirror the existing FirewallError fail-closed path exactly: a new pure probe module, a no-op-when-unwired ensure step, a guard branch that writes the durable stall marker, and the new reason registered in the marker enumeration. Discovered live during the CAM-175 ceremony (claude auth was loggedIn:false inside the container and nothing caught it before dispatch).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A new module src/supervisor/container-auth.ts provides the in-container claude auth probe, mirroring container-firewall.ts: buildAuthCheckExecArgv(containerName) returns the non-interactive argv ['exec', containerName, 'claude', 'auth', 'status', '--json'] (no -it, no sudo), applyContainerAuthCheck(containerName, spawnFn) runs it via spawnFn('docker', argv) and returns a discriminated {ok} result parsing the claude auth JSON loggedIn field (reusing the parse logic from src/commands/run-auth-preflight.ts), and class ContainerAuthError extends Error carries a stderrTail/message and sets name='ContainerAuthError', mirroring FirewallError. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/container-auth.test.ts] [oracle: grep -q "class ContainerAuthError" src/supervisor/container-auth.ts]

AC2: ensureWorkerContainer (src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts) gains an applyAuthCheckIfPresent(containerName, authCheckSpawnFn) step mirroring applyFirewallIfPresent: a complete no-op when the injected authCheckSpawnFn is undefined (host mode), otherwise it runs the probe and throws ContainerAuthError on loggedIn!==true; it is called unconditionally after applyConfigIfPresent and before the final return so a reused running container that lost its OAuth token is still caught. The authCheckSpawnFn seam is added to EnsureWorkerContainerOptions and wired from spawnSync in makeProductionEnsureContainerFn. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts] [oracle: grep -q "applyAuthCheckIfPresent" src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts]

AC3: runContainerEnsureGuard (src/commands/sidecar.ts) catches ContainerAuthError and mirrors the FirewallError path exactly (NOT the ContainerConfigError/ToolchainMismatchError paths, which write no marker): it writes the durable stall marker .claude/.cam-sidecar-stalled.json via writeSidecarStalledMarker with reason 'container-auth-unavailable' and detail from the error, then returns true so boot aborts before the loop and no worker is dispatched. [oracle: bun test test/commands/sidecar-auth.test.ts] [oracle: grep -q "container-auth-unavailable" src/commands/sidecar.ts]

AC4: The new reason is registered in src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts: 'container-auth-unavailable' is added to both the SidecarStalledReason type and the VALID_REASONS array (and the JSDoc reason list) so readSidecarStalledMarker round-trips the new marker instead of rejecting it as an unrecognized discriminator. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.test.ts] [oracle: grep -q "container-auth-unavailable" src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts]
AC5: Host mode and the claude backend path are unchanged (host-mode ensure stays a no-op, all existing tests stay green) and the full gate is green. [oracle: bun run check:all]
gotchas: Mirror the FirewallError path (sidecar.ts:3344-3354, writes the marker), NOT ContainerConfigError (:3355-3360) or ToolchainMismatchError (:3361-3367), which deliberately do NOT write a marker. CAM-396 requires a durable marker, so the auth branch must copy the FirewallError branch, not the nearest sibling.

Load-bearing: src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts SidecarStalledReason type (:33) AND the VALID_REASONS array (:47) AND the JSDoc list (:26-33) must all gain 'container-auth-unavailable'. If VALID_REASONS is not updated, readSidecarStalledMarker rejects the new marker as an unrecognized discriminator and silently returns null (:70-72).

The apply* DI-seam pattern (applyFirewallIfPresent :198-207, applyConfigIfPresent :218-232): the ensure step takes an OPTIONAL injected spawnFn; undefined => complete no-op (host mode); the pure applyContainer* helper returns a discriminated {ok} union and NEVER throws; the typed error is thrown in the apply* wrapper. Wire the production closure from spawnSync in makeProductionEnsureContainerFn (:439-508, mirror :463-491) and pass it into the ensureWorkerContainer call (:497-506).

Slot applyAuthCheckIfPresent AFTER applyConfigIfPresent (ensure-container.ts:417) and BEFORE the final return (:419): auth depends on the config step having repaired /home/bun/.claude ownership first, and it must run unconditionally so a reused running container (running->reuse branch, no docker call) that lost its OAuth token is still caught.

The probe is non-interactive: argv ['exec', name, 'claude', 'auth', 'status', '--json'] (no -it, no sudo), driven by spawnFn('docker', argv) exactly like applyContainerFirewall (container-firewall.ts:91-92). Do NOT reuse dockerExecWrap (docker-exec.ts:34, it builds an interactive '-it' STRING for tmux pane dispatch, wrong for a spawnSync probe). Reuse parseAuthJson/loggedIn from run-auth-preflight.ts:44-56,125.

No production code reads .cam-sidecar-stalled.json today (ADR-0026's boot surface is not yet wired to readSidecarStalledMarker); the enumeration update is still load-bearing for the round-trip test and any future reader. sidecar-liveness-watch.ts:110-113 is a second producer (reason 'sidecar-died').

Test DI patterns to reuse: test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts (makeRecordingSpawnFn returning a non-zero exitCode to simulate a failing docker exec, no real container); test/commands/sidecar-firewall.test.ts (runSidecar with ensureContainerFn that throws + a runSidecarLoopFn spy proving the loop never runs, and readSidecarStalledMarker asserting reason/detail/writtenAt) as the template for a new test/commands/sidecar-auth.test.ts; test/commands/run-auth-preflight.test.ts (makeFakeAuthSpawn + loggedInPayload) for the auth JSON fake.
domainTerms: container ensure-guard: runContainerEnsureGuard (src/commands/sidecar.ts:3331-3370), which ensures the cam-worker container is healthy before the sidecar loop dispatches any worker in worker_isolation=container mode; returning true aborts boot before the loop (fail-closed).
fail-closed preflight: an ensure step that throws a typed error caught by the guard, which writes a durable stall marker and returns true so no worker is ever dispatched.

container auth-preflight: the new ensure step probing claude auth INSIDE the container via docker exec claude auth status --json and parsing loggedIn, distinct from the host-side checkClaudeAuth in run-auth-preflight.ts.
